name: Question 11
problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=-i+j+\sqrt{2}\,k,\,{q}^{′}(1)=2\,j+\sqrt{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{2(1)}{({1}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{1}{{1}^{2}+1}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-i+j+\sqrt{2}\,k)+\frac{1}{2}(2\,j+\sqrt{2}\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =|\frac{1}{2}|\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(i+j)}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{2}q(1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-i+j+\sqrt{2}\,k)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(-1+1+0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by T(t)=1t2+1⋅q(t). Find the principal normal vector at the point where t=1, if q(1)=−i+j+2k,q′(1)=2j+2k.

a
 12(i+j)
b
 16(−2j+2k)
c
 15(i+j−2k)
d
 13(2i−j+2k)
e
 12(i−k)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate T′(t) and evaluate it at t=1:

T′(t)=ddt(1t2+1⋅q(t))=ddt(1t2+1)⋅q(t)+1t2+1⋅ddt(q(t))=−2t(t2+1)2⋅q(t)+1t2+1⋅q′(t)T′(1)=−2(1)(12+1)2⋅q(1)+112+1⋅q′(1)=−12(−i+j+2k)+12(2j+2k)=12(i+j)

Next, we find the magnitude of T′(1):

‖T′(1)‖=|12|(1)2+(1)2+(0)2=22

Finally, we normalize T′(1) and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where t=1:

N(1)=T′(1)‖T′(1)‖=12(i+j)(22)=12(i+j)

Note that when we find the scalar product of N and T at the point where t=1, we get

T(1)⋅N(1)=12q(1)⋅12(i+j)=12(−i+j+2k)⋅12(i+j)=122(−1+1+0)=0.✓
